articles.title: Fake wide receivers to undercover stings: did the 49ers have the wildest NFL preseason of all time?
articles.summary: A large part of San Francisco’s summer was a literal car crash. On the positive side, they have so far avoided their usual list of crushing injuries. The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers have trekked to Australia for this week’s NFL season opener in Melbourne.
body: It’s been smooth sailing for the Rams, with their collection of playmakers growing by the day. It’s a very different story for the 49ers: facing Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, not to mention the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks, at least twice this season is the least of their problems. Their offseason has been more than lightly turbulent: it’s been batshit crazy.

The history of NFL scandals is Mariana Trench deep, and every season a unique calamity pops up. Meet Daejon Love, 49ers wide receiver, wealthy investor and a Casanova on the prowl. At least that’s what the 26 women Love allegedly defrauded out of $1.3m are said to have believed. Love, who it turns out is decidedly not a San Francisco 49er, was arrested last month by the FBI and has been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. It’s unclear what is more bonkers: Love’s apparent audacity or the fact that none of the women he is said to have defrauded appear to have googled their new “NFL player” boyfriend.

The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers have trekked to Australia for this week’s NFL season opener in Melbourne.

articles.title: Champions League is fertile ground for new managers – but knowhow could be key later on
articles.summary: Luis Enrique, Vincent Kompany and Mikel Arteta are among the favourites to lead their sides to victory, but more recent appointments should not be counted out. A delve into the history of the Champions League shows that managers can and do win in their first season at a club, but also that…
body: It gets under way on Tuesday with 14 of the 36 clubs led by managers who have been in the role for less than a year. It cannot match the turnover of the Premier League, in which 11 of 20 managers were appointed in 2026, but the tenures of the head coaches involved this season break down neatly.

There are also 14 managers who have been in charge for at least two years. This leaves eight in the middle, who qualified for the Champions League in their first full season at their club and now get to show what they can do.

Being new to a team is no barrier to winning. Many who have led sides to the ultimate European club glory did so in their first campaign. Both Chelsea’s Champions League triumphs were secured by managers who got the job the same year. Carlo Ancelotti began both of his stints at Real Madrid by helping them to become champions of Europe in his year one, and in between Zinedine Zidane won three Champions League trophies on the bounce when he first managed the club.

articles.title: Mourinho, Inter and Champions League: Can he deliver again at Real Madrid?
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho begins his second Real Madrid spell in the Champions League against former club Inter Milan, 16 years after winning the trophy with Inter at the Bernabeu. Will he finally deliver European glory in Madrid?
body: There are few more fitting opponents for Jose Mourinho's return to the Champions League as Real Madrid boss than Inter Milan.
Sixteen years ago, Mourinho stood in the Santiago Bernabeu and lifted the trophy after leading Inter to a 2-0 victory over Bayern Munich in the 2010 final.
It was his second Champions League triumph, after Porto in 2004, and the final match of his Inter reign.
Days later, he was appointed Real Madrid manager for his first spell at the club.

articles.title: Newcastle admit they started planning for Eddie Howe’s exit at start of year
articles.summary: Manager made surprise decision to step down in July. Sporting director disappointed to lose Bruno Guimarães. Newcastle’s sporting director, Ross Wilson, has revealed he began planning at the start of this year for Eddie Howe’s departure.
body: “Eddie leaving didn’t feel chaotic and it didn’t feel painful,” said Wilson, who arrived on Tyneside from Nottingham Forest. “Eddie would be the first to tell you that. I came here 10 or 11 months ago and I’ve been planning in the background for a managerial change over eight or nine of those months. That doesn’t mean we were always going to go to Matthias, but he was always part of our planning.”

When Wilson began making contingency plans, Howe seemed more likely to be poached than to resign or be dismissed. Yet Newcastle’s 12th-placed finish last season raised questions about his future and, after the sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, Howe decided he wanted out.
“Big respect to Eddie for the job he did for us over a long period of time,” Wilson said. “He did a wonderful job bringing that trophy [the 2025 Carabao Cup]. He’s a club legend, for sure.”

No one had envisaged parting with Howe three weeks before the season. “Clearly the timing wasn’t planned,” Wilson said. “But the reason we could move so quickly was because we’d been preparing for a number of months.

articles.title: Cricket in Australia set for dramatic shake-up after BBL privatisation plan approved
articles.summary: Sales process launched for Melbourne Renegades. NSW and Queensland had been fiercely against bold plan. Cricket Australia say opening up the Big Bash League to private investors is in the best long-term interests of the sport in this country.
body: Privatisation in the BBL has been approved, just months after Cricket Victoria controversially decided it wanted to merge the Melbourne Stars and Melbourne Renegades.
Despite NSW and Queensland being fiercely against privatisation, CA is forging ahead with the bold concept. Tasmania, Victoria and Western Australia have long been in support of the decision.
CA chairman Mike Baird stressed Australian cricket would retain control of international scheduling, player availability, the BBL salary cap and branding proposals.
“By opening the door to private investment in the Big Bash Leagues, Cricket Australia is taking a deliberate step to strengthen and secure the long-term future of the game,” Baird said.

articles.title: What drives McCoy after second big crash in 13 months?
articles.summary: After he injured his back in his second big crash in 13 months, Gary McCoy speaks to the BBC Bikes podcast about his recovery and drive to return to racing.
body: When Gary McCoy slid off his bike at the Isle of Man TT in June, he had two seconds to process what was about to happen.
The Northern Ireland road racer ended up in hospital with five broken vertebrae in his back, one of which was crushed, and a broken shoulder blade.
Just 13 months earlier, McCoy had another big crash at the North West 200 which left him with serious injuries.
On that occasion, a following rider crashed into McCoy from behind approaching Mill Road roundabout and he was left with a bleed in the brain, a punctured lung and 22 broken bones.

articles.title: Non-league to Champions League: The Porto boss out to stun Man City
articles.summary: Porto boss Francesco Farioli is one of the most highly regarded young managers and on Tuesday he takes charge in the Champions League for the first time.
body: The 37-year-old led Porto to the Portuguese title last season and is now preparing to take charge of his first Champions League match as a manager against Manchester City at the Estadio do Dragao on Tuesday.
Leading a team out in Europe's premier club competition might still feel a long time coming for Farioli, who was linked with the vacancies at Chelsea, Liverpool and Rangers last season.
However, Farioli, who began his managerial journey in Turkey in 2021 with Fatih Karagumruk and then Alanyaspor, opted to renew his contract instead and is certain he made the right choice.
"I don't feel I could be in a better place," he told BBC Sport.

articles.title: 15 Years of our Stadium | Statistics, records and key figures of the Bianconeri
articles.summary: Fifteen years, hundreds of matches, goals, victories and star players. Since its opening in September 2011, the Stadium has become Juventus’ home and one of the iconic venues in the club’s recent...
body: The Men’s First Team have played 389 official matches at the Stadium, recording 282 wins, 76 draws and just 31 defeats. That’s a win rate of over 72 per cent.
In these matches, Juventus have scored 778 goals, conceded 265 and kept a clean sheet on 195 occasions: practically one clean sheet every two matches.
Serie A naturally accounts for the largest share, with 287 matches, followed by the UEFA Champions League with 59, the Italian Cup with 35 and the UEFA Europa League with 8.

The first official goal was scored by Stephan Lichtsteiner against Parma on 11 September 2011. A few weeks later, on 2 October against Milan, the first brace at the Stadium was scored by Claudio Marchisio.

articles.title: Newcastle chief: Summer was 'not chaotic' with Howe exit prepared for
articles.summary: Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson says they were "prepared for a number of months" for Eddie Howe's exit in a summer that "never felt chaotic".
body: Howe's shock resignation in July led to the swift appointment of Matthias Jaissle, who has enjoyed an unbeaten start to his reign.
Howe's exit was part of a turbulent summer for the Magpies which also included the departures of key players Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.
Toon chief Wilson revealed Howe's resignation was not "painful" because of their Jaissle contingency, but Guimaraes' £75m move to Arsenal was not "part of the plan".
Wilson said: "Eddie is an exceptionally talented coach and at some point that meant he was probably going to do something else and we had to be prepared for that.

articles.title: “It’s normal” Kessie breaks silence on snubbing Juventus for Atalanta
articles.summary: Franck Kessie was widely expected to move to Juventus this summer as a free agent, and he tried his best to make the transfer happen. The midfielder waited patiently for Juve to offload some players and make a move for him, believing the opportunity to join the Bianconeri was within reach.
body: It was a move that would have represented an exception for Juventus, as the club had previously decided against signing players who had had a spell in the Saudi Pro League. Kessie remains a top player, as he showed at the World Cup, and Juve were keen to add him to their squad during the transfer window.

Despite the interest from Juve, Kessie ultimately ended up at Atalanta. La Dea was his first club when he moved to Europe as a youngster, and he is happy to return to a familiar environment after his unsuccessful attempt to join the Bianconeri.

Kessie was reportedly close to a move to Juve before rejecting their approach. The Bianconeri had been expected to return with a better offer for his signature, but the midfielder was announced as a new Atalanta player before that could happen.
“It’s normal that when you’re free, there are lots of teams interested in you. I spoke to other teams, but when Atalanta came along, I had no doubts. It was a choice of the heart, an easy decision.”

articles.title: Should England rotate bowlers or be ruthless in final Pakistan Test?
articles.summary: As a Test summer during which English cricket appeared to be in crisis nears its end, Joe Root's side go into their final fixture against Pakistan with the only major talking point being whether the bowling attack will be rotated.
body: Barring the discovery of any more England off-field issues before the start of the third Test at Edgbaston on Wednesday, it's Pakistan making all the noise after sacking their head coach and replacing seven members of their touring squad following defeats at Headingley and Lord's.

Brydon Carse remains absent from England's 15-player group at Edgbaston after the fast bowler was briefly arrested following an incident outside a Derby nightclub in August. Fellow quick Matthew Fisher has been dropped, but the rest of the group were all part of the squad at Lord's last time out.
With a series victory sealed, England could choose to give some of their cross-format players a rest ahead of upcoming white-ball contests with Sri Lanka.
If the third Test were to go all five days, the first of three T20 internationals would start just two days later, before three 50-over matches follow later in September.

articles.title: How Calafiori has become 'the best left-back in the league by far'
articles.summary: Riccardo Calafiori returns to Italy with Arsenal this week - and he's a very different player compared to the one who departed for England two years ago.
body: When Arsenal came in for Calafiori, he was regularly playing at centre-back at Bologna. Those who guided his career had doubts about whether he could reach the highest level as a left-back.
But now, Calafiori is not just thriving as a left-back for the Premier League champions. "He's the best left-back in the league by far," says Jamie Carragher.

As well as being part of an imperious Arsenal defence, the Italian has started this season on fire in front of goal, scoring in the Community Shield win over Manchester City and getting assists in the league victories over Coventry and Aston Villa.
VAR spotting an offside Ezri Konsa denied Calafiori getting on the scoresheet against Chelsea, but the Italian did have a crucial role in Arsenal's winning goal, scored by Martin Odegaard.
